name: Deindex Unpublished Files
description: Moves an unpublished media entity's file to private storage (or renames it .ht_) and restores it on publish, so unpublished files stop being publicly downloadable.
project_description: Deindex Unpublished Files targets a long-standing Drupal gap: unpublishing a media entity hides the media, but the underlying file, if stored in public://, remains directly downloadable at its URL. This module reacts to the media publish-state change (hook_media_presave) and physically relocates the file so it is no longer served publicly. Two operator-selectable modes exist: 'move' relocates unpublished public:// files into private://unpublishedfiles/ (served only through Drupal's file-access checks) and moves them back to public:// on republish; 'prefix' renames the file with a leading .ht_ (a dotfile blocked by Drupal's default .htaccess / recommended nginx rules) and strips the prefix on republish. It only affects media types that contain a file, image, or svg_image field. The module also ships an admin 'Media usage overview' page (Content > Unpublish media by usage) backed by a MediaUsageInspector service that scans nodes and other content entities (including CKEditor embeds, paragraphs, and revision references) to find media used only by unpublished content, with a bulk-unpublish action. Despite the SEO-sounding name and package, the mechanism is physical file relocation, not an HTTP header: the module does NOT emit an X-Robots-Tag header and does NOT implement hook_file_download, so it does not itself make any file-access grant/deny decision.
